primitives.name: Temporal Data Consistency
primitives.verbatim_quote: All game data must have `commence_time` in the future (or < 3hr ago for live) 2.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'t_{commence}': 'time of game commencement (seconds since Unix epoch)', 't_{now}': 'current system time (seconds since Unix epoch)'}
primitives.assumptions: Game data is valid iff t_{commence} > t_{now} - 10800 seconds.
primitives.breakdown_regime: t_{commence} <= t_{now} - 10800 implies stale or invalid data.

layer2.mapping: Temporal filtering in GSI mirrors state validation in GSE; both enforce causality through time-bound data.
layer2.telemetry: Time difference between commence and current time.

primitives.name: Ingestion Run Traceability
primitives.verbatim_quote: All picks must trace back to an ingestion run ID 4.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'R_{id}': 'unique ingestion run identifier (UUID string)', 'P_{id}': 'pick identifier (UUID string)'}
primitives.assumptions: Each pick P_{id} has a deterministic R_{id} link.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Missing R_{id} in P_{id} implies traceability failure.

layer2.mapping: Traceability enables retroactive auditability in GSI; GSE uses it for pick revalidation.

primitives.name: Freshness Policy
primitives.verbatim_quote: GET /v4/sports/{sport}/events — get events (games) ``` ### Response Freshness Policy - Data older than 60
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'t_{fetched}': 'timestamp of data fetch (seconds since Unix epoch)', 't_{stale}': 'threshold for stale data (seconds)', 't_{now}': 'current system time (seconds since Unix epoch)'}
primitives.assumptions: Data is fresh iff t_{now} - t_{fetched} < 60.

layer2.mapping: Freshness policy in GSI aligns with GSE's data-driven decision engine; both reject outdated inputs.
layer2.telemetry: Age of fetched data in seconds.

Ingestion run traceability ensures all decisions can be audited back to their origin, forming a chain of accountability. Freshness policy acts as a dynamic filter that rejects stale data, maintaining signal integrity. These primitives form a dual structure: one enforcing logical consistency (temporal), the other ensuring operational robustness (traceability/freshness). Failure modes include temporal drift (e.g., clock skew), traceability gaps (e.g., missing run IDs), and stale data ingestion (e.g., beyond 60s threshold). Dualities emerge in how these constraints interact: temporal validity gates traceability, while traceability supports freshness checks. The system’s resilience depends on these interlocking constraints preventing cascading failures.
